Commit `a9c1ded` rewrote the method and dropped the `arena.inArena(p)` check from the `isRunning()` branch — previously the check `!arena.inArena((Player) event.getEntity())` (short-circuit return) covered all cases, but the refactor removed that check for the "arena is running" branch entirely, only leaving `lockFoodLevel`. Let me confirm the full commit details and surrounding context.

content.text:
This confirms the full picture: commit `a9c1ded` restructured `onFoodLevelChange` to handle lobby/spec players separately (using `inLobby`/`inSpec`), but in doing so dropped the `arena.inArena(p)` guard for the "arena is running" branch — leaving only `lockFoodLevel`, so food level changes for *any* player (not just those actually in the arena) would get cancelled while the arena is running. The bug-fixing commit `5058c479` simply re-adds `arena.inArena(p) &&` to that condition.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: a9c1ded76ed1fc157add8ef73565bd6112967bf1

## Reasoning
(1) I ran `git log -p -L` on the affected line range of `ArenaListener.java` to trace the history of the `onFoodLevelChange` method before the fix commit. This showed the method's evolution through exactly two prior states.

(2) The original implementation guarded the whole method with `if (!(event.getEntity() instanceof Player) || !arena.inArena((Player) event.getEntity())) return;` before checking `lockFoodLevel`. Commit `a9c1ded76ed1fc157add8ef73565bd6112967bf1` refactored this to split behavior between "arena running" and "lobby/spec" cases (adding lobby/spec food locking), but when rewriting the "running" branch it only kept `if (lockFoodLevel) { event.setCancelled(true); }`, dropping the `arena.inArena(p)` check entirely. This meant that while an arena was running, any player's food level change could be cancelled if `lockFoodLevel` was true, even if that player wasn't actually in the arena.

(3) The bug-fixing commit's diff is a minimal, targeted restoration of exactly that missing condition — changing `if (lockFoodLevel)` back to `if (arena.inArena(p) && lockFoodLevel)` — with no other logic changes, which strongly corroborates that `a9c1ded` is the sole origin of the regression.

I'm confident in this identification; the `git log -L` history for this exact line range only contains these two commits between file creation and the fix, leaving little ambiguity.
